items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: During this time in the '40s that I made that album with I thought was a terrific album, the one with Ellis Larkins and the trio.

ctx.x: During this time in the '40s that I made that album with I thought was a terrific album, the one with Ellis Larkins and the trio. And the material in the recording itself was so poor that the disc jockeys couldn't play it. The needle just skipped all over the place. And there were a lot of people not recording because even the recording companies were standing at a standstill. So they didn't have the material to make the record with. There's a possibility, I'm not sure but a lot of stuff that was being played was…
And there was the combination of both, the ASCAP thing.

items.q: some of the best things that I feel that I made were the next group of things I made with Ellis Larkin.

ctx.x: But at this particular point, it didn't matter. I mean I was already established.

And this didn't make much difference. I mean, I made the records -- maybe somebody bought them for what they were worth -- but the real -- some of the best things that I feel that I made were the next group of things I made with Ellis Larkin.
